threat_event: Attacker signs in through the lock vendor's always-on remote support tool, moves to the front desk PC, and installs malware that captures keyed card numbers and security codes
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Always-on remote tool with a password shared by the vendor's technicians and no MFA; flat office network; keyed card entry on a general-purpose PC; no EDR
existing_controls: MSP firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic; antivirus on PCs; P2PE terminals
treatment_plan: Turn the lock tool off between sessions and start sessions from the motel side with a one-time code; written remote access and incident notice terms with the lock vendor; separate networks for payments, the lock system, and the office; EDR; stop keyed entry on PCs (P03 redesign)

threat_event: Phishing email to the shared front desk mailbox installs an information stealer on the front desk PC; PMS and email credentials are stolen
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared Windows login with automatic sign-in; shared mailbox password without MFA; no awareness training; front desk PC used for web browsing
existing_controls: Suite spam filtering; antivirus
treatment_plan: Training at hire and yearly with phishing examples; named accounts with MFA for every PMS and mailbox user; EDR; block web browsing on the front desk PC except approved sites

threat_event: Card authorization forms stored in the shared mailbox are taken by anyone who gets the mailbox password
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: About 640 emails with card numbers since 2021, about 260 with security codes; shared password never changed when staff leave; no MFA
existing_controls: Suite spam filtering
treatment_plan: Delete the emails with security codes now; purge the rest after billing checks; stop accepting card forms by 2026-11-30 (pay-by-link instead); named mailboxes with MFA

threat_event: Printed crew card forms in the open front desk binder are copied or taken
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Binder unlocked under the counter since 2021; forms include security codes; no log of who handles it
existing_controls: Front desk staffed 24 hours
treatment_plan: Lock the binder in the back office now; shred forms after billing checks; no paper card forms after 2026-11-30

threat_event: A front office user displays OTA virtual card numbers and misuses them
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: All 5 front office users hold the 'view full card number' permission; clerks display cards routinely; no review of display logs
existing_controls: Background checks on front desk hires; PMS logs every display
treatment_plan: Remove the permission from everyone except the Owner-Manager; charge virtual cards through the PMS without display; weekly review of display logs

threat_event: A former employee signs in to the PMS after leaving
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No termination checklist; 2 former employees' PMS accounts found active in P07 testing (no sign-ins after their last day)
existing_controls: PMS administrators can disable users at once
treatment_plan: Last-day checklist covering the PMS, email, lock system, shared passwords, and keys; monthly account reconciliation

threat_event: Actions on the shared front desk login and mailbox cannot be traced to a person, so misuse or mistakes go unexplained
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One shared Windows login with automatic sign-in; one shared mailbox password
existing_controls: Named PMS logins
treatment_plan: Named Windows accounts with fast user switching; named mailboxes with delegated access to a front desk inbox

threat_event: Malware on any office device reaches the payment terminals, lock system, and CCTV because the office network is flat
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: PCs, terminals, printer, CCTV recorder, and tablets share one network; outbound traffic unrestricted
existing_controls: Guest Wi-Fi separated; inbound traffic blocked
treatment_plan: MSP creates separate networks for terminals, the lock system and CCTV, and office PCs, with deny-by-default rules

threat_event: Ransomware or a disk failure on the back office PC destroys the door lock database, so no new key cards can be encoded
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Lock database excluded from the backup job (found in P07 testing); no restore test; single PC hosts the lock software
existing_controls: Locks keep working with existing cards; mechanical override keys for staff
treatment_plan: Add the lock database to the nightly backup; restore-test it with the lock vendor; keep a sealed set of emergency key cards; ask the lock vendor for a written rebuild procedure

threat_event: PMS vendor outage lasts longer than the 2-hour check-in RTO
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single SaaS system of record; vendor RTO of 4 hours exceeds BP-01's 2 hours
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 availability commitments; printed arrivals list each night
treatment_plan: Paper check-in kit at the desk; confirm offline key encoding works without the PMS interface; ask for RTO and RPO in the contract at renewal

threat_event: Internet outage stops the PMS, the payment terminals, and OTA connections
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One internet line; no failover
existing_controls: Owner-Manager's phone hotspot (manual)
treatment_plan: MSP installs a cellular failover router for the office network; contingency plan step for the front desk

threat_event: Backed-up files and mailboxes cannot be restored when needed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No restore test since setup in 2024; 30-day versions that are not immutable
existing_controls: Nightly backup with MFA on the console
treatment_plan: First restore test (including the lock database) by 2026-10-31, then quarterly; enable immutable versions

threat_event: The dynamic pricing tool raises rates sharply during a declared state of emergency (evacuees), exposing the motel to price gouging enforcement and lasting reputational harm
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Rates publish automatically with no ceiling and no emergency rule; in the 2025 hurricane evacuation, rates rose 61% above the 30-day average for 2 nights
existing_controls: Owner-Manager can override rates in the PMS
treatment_plan: Ceiling and daily change limits in the tool; emergency mode that freezes rates at or below the 30-day pre-declaration average during a declaration; Owner-Manager approval for any increase (P10)

threat_event: The roadside sign, website banner, and phone quotes show rates without the mandatory $6 fee, inviting FTC enforcement and guest complaints
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Fee added only in the booking engine and at check-in; staff script and signs never updated; one OTA shows the base rate because the fee is not mapped as mandatory in its channel feed (found in P10)
existing_controls: Booking engine shows total price since May 2025
treatment_plan: Show the total price on the sign, banner, and phone script; map the fee as mandatory in all 3 OTA feeds; check all price displays monthly

threat_event: The acquirer finds the motel non-compliant (wrong SAQ), adding fees or penalties, and the motel bears card brand costs after any breach
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2025 SAQ P2PE signed although not eligible; no scope document; keyed entry and stored card data
existing_controls: Acquirer agreed the 2026 approach on 2026-08-19
treatment_plan: Complete the redesign by 2026-11-30; scope document; SAQ P2PE plus SAQ A by 2026-12-31 (SAQ D if the redesign slips past 2026-12-15)

threat_event: Staff do not recognize or report a card compromise, so the acquirer's 24-hour and Visa's 3-day clocks are missed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident response plan before 2026-08; no reporting rule; no training
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: POL-03 and the P08 runbook; reporting card at the front desk; covered in training; tabletop exercise

threat_event: A caller posing as a guest, an OTA, or vendor support talks a clerk into giving out guest details, a room number, or a key
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No caller verification rule; night shift works alone
existing_controls: Staff do not give room numbers over the phone by habit (not written)
treatment_plan: Written caller verification rule; never give room numbers or card details by phone; call vendors back on known numbers; training

threat_event: A breach of the PMS exposes ID numbers of guests from as far back as 2021, enlarging the notice population
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: About 14,000 ID scans and 31,000 profiles kept indefinitely; PMS purge settings off
existing_controls: PMS vendor security (SOC 2)
treatment_plan: Retention schedule: register data 2 years; ID scans deleted 30 days after checkout; turn on PMS purge settings

threat_event: A skimming overlay or swapped terminal at the front desk captures card data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No device list with serial numbers; no inspections; staff not trained to spot tampering
existing_controls: Front desk staffed 24 hours; terminals in view of cameras
treatment_plan: Device list with serial numbers; weekly inspection log at the night audit; staff training; follow the P2PE Instruction Manual

threat_event: Compromise of the MSP's remote management platform reaches every PC; the MSP has no recovery commitment
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MSP tool has administrator access to all PCs; no review of MSP security; contract has a 4-business-hour response time only
existing_controls: MSP states it uses MFA (not evidenced)
treatment_plan: Yearly MSP security review (MFA evidence, technician list); contract terms for incident notice within 24 hours and a recovery time at renewal

threat_event: Background-check reports kept in an office drawer are disposed of without shredding
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Reports printed and filed; no disposal procedure
existing_controls: Cross-cut shredder in the back office
treatment_plan: Accepted: few reports a year and a shredder already in use; POL-04 adds a shred-after-hire-decision rule at no cost

threat_event: A hurricane cuts power and access for several days, or brings an evacuee surge the front desk cannot handle
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No IT contingency plan; one internet line; lock system on one PC
existing_controls: Building hurricane checklist (shutters, generator for the office and lobby)
treatment_plan: Short contingency plan: generator circuit check for the office network and back office PC; paper check-in kit; emergency key cards; evacuee pricing rule (R-013)

threat_event: The Owner-Manager's laptop is lost or stolen
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptop travels off site
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; no card data stored; MSP can wipe
treatment_plan: Accepted: encrypted personal information is not personal information under Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)2.; residual risk Low
